xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3340: Dashboard: Review action should open a submenu to pick review mode (Full / Quick / None)

plan.title: Dashboard: Review action should open a submenu to pick review mode (Full / Quick / None)
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: Requesting a review and choosing its mode are two disjoint, silent dashboard interactions: the Review action dispatches with the already-resolved mode and shows no feedback, and the Policies mode chip's save swallows non-OK responses. On 2026-07-30 the operator clicked Review and FULL on MIN-908 and neither took effect; the review had to be dispatched from the CLI.
narratives.Proposal: Give the requestReview registry action a Full / Quick / None submenu on every surface (grouped, context, and — via a new popover on the primary-strip ActionButton — the kanban strip). Selecting a mode POSTs { reviewMode } to the existing trigger route, which persists the mode through the record write door (updateIssueRecord) synchronously before responding, then dispatches; dispatch keeps reading the mode through resolveReviewMode. A success toast names the chosen mode, persist failures fail the HTTP response, and IssuePolicyStrip.save gains an error toast. Full design, before/after snippets, and decisions: .pan/drafts/PAN-3340.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No current-mode indicator inside the submenu (would need a per-row GET /api/review/:id/config fetch).
- No change to background dispatch failure surfacing beyond the existing reviewStatus.reviewNotes + pending-operation machinery.
- No change to canRequestReview gating, the pan review CLI surface, or POST /api/review/:issueId/config behavior.
- No issue-action registry keys added, renamed, or removed; the dead 'Review & Test' button in WorkspaceStatusOverview.tsx stays dead.

autoDecisions.summary: Single POST: the trigger route accepts an optional reviewMode and persists it via the record write door before responding, instead of the frontend POSTing /api/review/:id/config then /trigger.
autoDecisions.rationale: Atomic ordering is guaranteed server-side and a mode-persist failure becomes a synchronous non-200 the frontend can surface; a two-POST dance has a partial-failure window.

autoDecisions.summary: The primary-strip ActionButton opens a popover when view.submenu exists, rather than click-dispatching with the current mode.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for the Review action itself to be a submenu; a strip button that still dispatches silently on click would preserve the exact interaction that bit the operator.

autoDecisions.summary: No current-mode checkmark in the submenu.
autoDecisions.rationale: It would require a GET /api/review/:id/config per rendered row on kanban/board surfaces; the Policies strip remains the mode display.

autoDecisions.summary: Background dispatch failures stay on the existing reviewNotes / pending-operation surface.
autoDecisions.rationale: In scope is making the click verifiably take effect: validation and mode persistence move before the 200 response; spawn health is already visible via the spawned agent row and review status.

autoDecisions.summary: Plain invoke() of requestReview still dispatches with the resolved mode (no body); registry key, testid, and gating unchanged.
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps programmatic/test paths working and lets the no-loss parity tests pass unmodified.

autoDecisions.summary: Submenu labels carry hints: 'Full — 4-reviewer convoy', 'Quick — single pass (default)', 'None — skip AI review'.
autoDecisions.rationale: The pick must be self-explanatory without opening docs; 'None' especially must state that AI review is skipped.

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/server/routes/workspaces/review-pipeline.ts, add an exported pure helper parseRequestedReviewMode(body) that returns { ok: true, mode? } for 'quick'|'full'|'none' (absent/null field → no mode) and { ok: false, error } otherwise. In the trigger route handler, reject invalid modes with 400 right after readJsonBody (line ~131), and — after all existing early-exit guards and immediately before the '// Respond immediately' background IIFE (line ~252) — persist a valid mode synchronously via resolveProjectForIssue + updateIssueRecord (dynamic-import pattern from review-control.ts:713-718), returning 500 without dispatching if persistence throws. Add unit tests for the pure helper in __tests__/review-pipeline-review-mode.test.ts following the review-pipeline-dirty-gate.test.ts style. Exact before/after snippets: .pan/drafts/PAN-3340.md WI-1.

items.title: parseRequestedReviewMode returns { ok: true, mode } for each of quick/full/none, returns { ok: true } with no mode for absent or null fields, and rejects 'FULL', '', 123, and {} with an error naming the allowed values
Given a valid reviewMode body, the route persists record.reviewMode through updateIssueRecord before the 200 response, and returns 500 without dispatching when persistence throws

Given any early-exit guard triggers (invalid id, remote workspace, already-reviewed, already-merged, missing workspace, conflict gate), the route returns the guard response and persists nothing to the issue record
